title: Incremental runtime cutover guide + TF deprecations and compatibility log
body:
Purpose:
This is a practical, incremental cutover and rollback guide for Private (VPC / on-prem) customers during runtime and control-plane upgrades. It focuses on minimizing customer impact by using phased traffic routing, compatibility shims, and Terraform module deprecation steps. This document is a working draft — expect iteration after field tests and first customer runs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployments using the Redwood control plane + runtime package (on-prem bundle or VPC-managed nodes).
- Customers may be running mixed-version runtimes across pools; control plane version must be within one minor of runtime while cutover proceeds.
- Terraform is used for infra+config; we will deprecate older TF module inputs in favor of new variables in a 3-step approach.
- Rollbacks must be possible without data-plane token leaks and with no model weight inconsistencies.

High-level strategy (phased):
1) Prepare and validate compatibility shims (pre-cutover):
   - Build and publish a compatibility shim image that provides API routing for legacy client paths (/v1/legacy/generate -> /v1/generate) and that supports both old and new config keys.
   - Add feature-flag gating in the control plane so rollout can be toggled per-customer.
   - Smoke test shim locally and on an internal staging cluster that mirrors customer topology.

2) Terraform module deprecation plan (parallel):
   - Create new module variables with _v2 suffix (e.g., batch_settings_v2). Mark old inputs as deprecated in module docs and emit terraform warnings by adding validation rules.
   - Provide automated module migration snippet in CHANGELOG: sample sed/awk snippet and terraform state mv examples for resources renames.
   - Timeline: announce deprecation window (30 days), provide autoconversion script for common cases, then perform hard removal in next major release.

3) Canary pool upgrade (control plane + runtime):
   - Select minimal canary: one small customer or internal pool (1–2 nodes) with low traffic.
   - Steps: allocate canary node pool, apply new runtime image, roll control plane components in sequence (scheduler -> proxy -> control-plane-api), validate heartbeats and model manifests.
   - Validate: per-route latency (P50/P95), model loads, KV cache hit rates, tokenization parity tests.

4) Incremental traffic shift toward upgraded pool:
   - Use the smart routing policy: route 5% traffic to canary for 1 hour, 25% for 3 hours, 50% next day, 100% after 48 hours if no regressions.
   - Automated rollback trigger at each gate if error rate increases by > 2x baseline or P95 latency regresses > 30% for > 10 minutes.

Compatibility matrix and rule-of-thumb:
- Control plane X.Y -> runtime A.B: supported if control-plane minor version difference <= 1 and runtime supports API v1/v2 compatibility headers.
- If runtime introduces breaking API (rare), enable shim and force client version pinning until migration completes.

Validation and test suites (must be runnable by SRE/CS):
- Smoke tests: token generation (short prompt), streaming correctness, function-calling roundtrip, embedding generation, and reranking sanity.
- E2E tests: full prompt sequences including multi-turn chat, KV cache preservation across requests, and rolling restart resiliency.
- Golden prompt diff: run a curated set of 250 prompts comparing old vs new runtime; log token-level diffs and perceptual deltas.

Rollback playbook (fast path):
- When a gate triggers rollback:
  1) Pause traffic shift automation in the Console (route all traffic back to stable pool).
  2) For runtime nodes: trigger rolling rollback (kubectl set image back to stable image tag or revert instance template).
  3) For control plane: roll back the API server deployment only after runtime nodes are stable. Do NOT roll control plane first.
  4) Revert Terraform changes if infra-level drift occurred (terraform apply using stable state file). Use terraform state pull > backup-state.tfstate before reverting.
  5) Notify stakeholders via #private-deployments on Slack and create an incident note in the control-plane incident tracker.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- ErrRate: sustained > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Latency: P95 > 1.3x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Tokenization/model mismatch: any golden-prompt diff with > 4% token-level divergence for critical prompts.
- Resource anomalies: memory OOM or kernel panics detected on >1 node in pool.

Terraform-specific notes (practical tips):
- Resource rename pattern: when changing resource names, prefer state move approach. Example: terraform state mv module.runtime.aws_instance.old_name module.runtime.aws_instance.new_name. Document every state mv operation in the customer ticket.
- Input deprecation: we will add dynamic validation blocks that produce warnings (using terraform 1.5+) to guide customers before hard removal.
- Backward-compatible provider upgrades: test provider minor bumps in an isolated workspace; record provider_versions constraints in module's required_providers block.

Control plane compatibility shims (implementation sketch):
- shim-proxy image that intercepts legacy endpoints and rewrites headers/body into the new schema. Expose feature flags via /admin/flag endpoint.
- Health-checks: shim must respond to /live and /ready consistent with upstream readiness semantics so orchestration doesn't kill it accidentally.

Operational runbook checklist (pre-cutover):
- Confirm backups for artifact store (model artifacts and configs) are complete and verified (checksum).
- Generate and store a terraform state snapshot in S3/archive with date tag.
- Create customer communication draft and scheduled maintenance window (if applicable).
- Run golden-prompt suite and capture baseline metrics.
- Prepare rollback image tags and keep them in immutable registry with clear naming (e.g., runtime-20241104-stable).

Monitoring and observability (what to watch):
- Per-customer request rate, error rate, P50/P95 latency by route and model.
- Model caching metrics: KV cache hit-rate and prefix miss spikes.
- GPU utilization and memory headroom.
- Control plane API error rates and queue sizes.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: TF module variable name change accidentally breaks automated CI. Mitigation: ship autoconversion script and ensure CI runs plan against a duplicated workspace first.
- Risk: Sticky clients pinned to old API semantics. Mitigation: enable compat-shim and log all shim usage to find stragglers.
- Risk: State drift due to manual infra changes. Mitigation: require terraform apply to be the only path to change infra; enforce via a pre-apply gating job in CI.

Customer communication templates (short):
- Pre-upgrade: what we will change, expected rollout timeline, any required customer action (eg: terraform variable rename recommended).
- Post-upgrade: quick status, whether rollback occurred, link to incident notes, performance deltas.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default traffic ramp cadence for high-traffic customers (>10k rps). Proposed: slower ramp (1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with longer observation windows.
- Finalize module deprecation timeline and how we surface warnings in the Console.
- Add guided migration flow to the Console that can perform terraform variable translation via an export script.

Action items (owners):
- Diego: implement shim image and basic e2e tests (ETA: 2024-12-10).
- Rae: author terraform autoconversion script and sample state-move cookbook (ETA: 2024-12-18).
- Tomoko: build golden-prompt runbook and collect baseline results from staging clusters (ETA: 2024-12-05).
- Aisha: write customer comms and schedule first pilot (ETA: 2024-12-02).

Notes and retrospective checklist after first real cutover:
- Collect all golden prompt diffs, summarize top 10 regression prompts and attribution.
- Log any manual state-mv commands executed and reason for each.
- Update the TF module README with exact examples from the field run.

Appendix: quick commands (examples)
- Create a canary pool (example): kubectl apply -f canary-pool.yaml --context=staging
- Roll runtime image back: kubectl set image deployment/runtime runtime-container=registry.redwood/runtime:stable-20241104 -n customer-namespace
- Terraform snapshot: terraform state pull > backup-state-20241106.tfstate
- Terraform state move example: terraform state mv module.runtime.aws_instance.old_name module.runtime.aws_instance.new_name

If this doc is used for a customer-facing run, convert the Action items into a run-specific checklist and pin a copy to the customer ticket.

END OF DRAFT
